plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of silvery-green shrubs turn violet-blue, with slender flower spikes that hum with bees. The warm, herbal scent drifts across the fields on summer afternoons.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak bloom in mid-July
plants.funFact: The name lavender probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is the largest flower in the protea family. Its dinner-plate bloom is a crown of silky pink bracts around a downy center. It stands out in the cool, damp southern winter, when few other plants are in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: April to October, which includes the southern hemisphere winter
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change shape, because the protea family has so many different forms.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry golden, sun-tracking flower heads. Each head is a mass of tiny florets packed in a spiral and ringed with bright petal-like rays. In midsummer, whole fields seem to glow.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to August in temperate northern regions
plants.location: Gardens and farm fields across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers. Their seed spirals follow Fibonacci numbers.
